scope.direct: New optimizers, algorithmic variants, and substantively new optimizer/scheduler/state-management wrappers; includes theoretical and specialized algorithms, with scope and costs stated in summaries.
scope.weak: Substantive Muon theory, mechanisms, benchmarks, and implementation research without a newly proposed optimizer.
scope.resources: Muon technical explanations, implementations, and experimental resources.
scope.excluded: Physical muons; ordinary reuse of existing non-Muon optimizers; pure non-Muon analyses without new algorithm design; unrelated combinatorial/metaheuristic applications.

method: Search each calendar segment independently rather than using a last-week recency filter.
Screen complete native monthly cs.LG title lists where recorded; cross-check math.OC, date-filtered arXiv queries, official proceedings, and exact-month topic searches.
Inspect primary publication records and relevant full-text algorithm/experiment sections before retaining candidates.
Deduplicate against all three existing tables by canonical URL/arXiv ID and normalized title; retain original publication dates rather than revision or identifier months.
Verify substantive paper-linked official code before setting code URLs; do not turn empty stubs or baseline repositories into official implementations.

special_classification.reason: FINCH is explicitly labeled a new loss-adaptive learning-rate wrapper, not a new base optimizer.

BregTop belongs to May by original arXiv submission 2026-05-30, despite June identifier.

MACRO is a new single-loop manifold-constrained matrix optimizer; approximate tangency and radius/hardware costs explicitly stated.

PrePO is an independent AdamW/Muon trajectory-extrapolation-and-correction wrapper also tested in SFT, not merely a new policy objective. Three backward passes and limited/conditional speedups explicitly stated.

limitations: A systematic search within the recorded routes is not proof that every optimizer publication worldwide has been found.
Title screens can miss papers with atypical wording; the independent abstract-keyword Muon sweep mitigates this for Muon, but does not exhaust every non-Muon venue or category.
The catalog includes theory, specialized solvers, and wrappers. Inclusion is not a claim of suitability or superiority for large-language-model pretraining.
Reported gains retain their training scale, budget, tuning, numerical approximation, and uncertainty caveats; no global speedup claim is inferred from oracle complexity.
